Hartford
Creative Group, Inc. (“HFUS,” “we,” “us,” or “Company”) was originally incorporated in
the State of Nevada on April 2, 2008 under the name PhotoAmigo, Inc. It changed its name to Hartford Great Health Corp. on August 22,
2018. On May 11, 2024, the Company further changed its name to Hartford Creative Group, Inc.
Overview
The
Company is a media and marketing company. Following its exit from its legacy hospitality and early childhood education operations, the
Company has, since January 2024, concentrated on two principal lines of business: (i) social media advertising and related marketing
services in China, and (ii) a mini-drama content business, which includes a short-form drama streaming application launched in the United
States. The Company conducts its advertising operations through operating subsidiaries in China and supports its short-form drama application
with resources based in the United States.
Social
Media Advertising and Marketing Services.  The Company provides advertising placement and related marketing services on mainstream
social media platforms, including TikTok, Toutiao, Kwai, RED, WeChat, and Baidu. These services are conducted principally through its
subsidiaries Hartford ZY Culture Media (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (“HFZY”), ShaoXing HuoMao Network Technology Ltd. (“SXHM”),
which the Company acquired in June 2024, and Nanjing HaoYiPeng Information Technology Ltd. (“NJHY”), which HFZY established
in May 2025 to further expand the advertising business. In the advertising placement arrangement, the advertisements are published on
the media platforms selected by the customer; the Company does not control the underlying media traffic and therefore acts as an agent,
reporting placement revenue on a net basis. The Company intends to provide vertical integration services, including advertising creative
development, video production, editing, and advertising operations and campaign management. The Company also plans to develop overseas
TikTok advertising campaigns for domestic Chinese customers seeking to reach international markets.
Mini-Drama
Content Business.  Beginning in June 2025, the Company established a mini-drama content business that involves acquiring
non-exclusive licenses of mini-dramas, performing in-house editing, and licensing the completed content to customers. Because the Company
controls the license rights before they are transferred, is responsible for fulfilling the arrangement, and independently establishes
pricing, it acts as the principal in these transactions and recognizes the related revenue on a gross basis. This business is in an early,
developmental stage.
In
April 2026, the Company launched “YYYS,” a short-form drama streaming application. The application became available for testing
on April 28, 2026, was released on Google Play in the United States on May 6, 2026, and became available on the Apple App Store in the
United States on June 2, 2026. YYYS is positioned as a short-form drama platform aimed primarily at female users between the ages of
25 and 45 in the United States, and it focuses initially on romance and emotionally driven content, with additional genres such as suspense
and science fiction under evaluation. The Company offers its programming through a combination of internally produced and third-party
licensed content, draws on production resources in Los Angeles, and is evaluating the use of artificial intelligence-enabled tools in
content production and post-production. The Company expects to grow the YYYS content library over time.
The
Company intends to monetize the YYYS application through a one-time lifetime membership fee that provides users with access to platform
content and through an advertising-supported model for non-paying users, including reward-based video advertisements. The Company’s
user acquisition strategy combines organic traffic generated through social media platforms, such as YouTube, Facebook, and TikTok, with
paid user acquisition campaigns conducted through third-party advertising platforms. Following its initial launch in the United States,
the Company plans to pursue a phased international expansion strategy, subject to regulatory, operational, and commercial considerations.
There can be no assurance that these strategies will be successful.
